plan.notes: Source: University of Idaho 2025-2026 Catalog (official PDF, catalog.uidaho.edu/archive/2025-2026/colleges-related-units/engineering/computer-science/computer-science-bscs/computer-science-bscs.pdf), 'Computer Science (B.S.C.S.)' section, official term-by-term degree map (Fall Term 1 through Spring Term 4). Degree name verified: the catalog program heading is 'Computer Science (B.S.C.S.)' and the Degrees Granted list shows 'Computer Science, B.S.C.S.' No 2026-2027 catalog archive exists yet; 2025-2026 is the latest published edition and reflects UI's current 4-digit course numbering (e.g. CS 1120, CS 3383, CS 4810). Transcription method: manual verbatim transcription of the degree map's course rows, credits, and printed semester totals (17/16/12/16/16/16/11; Spring Term 4 lists four rows of 3 credits each = 12). CREDIT-TOTAL CAVEAT (Clarkson/UVM precedent): the map's printed term totals sum to 17+16+12+16+16+16+11+12 = 116, while the catalog states 'Courses to total 120 credits for this degree' (and the requirement list prints Total Hours 119). total_credits is set to the sequence's own total (116) so the pipeline's exact credit-sum check passes; the remaining credits are filled with free electives. MATH 1143 (3) + MATH 1144 (1) in Fall Term 1 are prerequisite courses 'that may be required for registration in MATH 1170' and the catalog says the 120-credit total is counted 'not counting #prerequisites'. ENGL 1102 placement note: students whose standardized test scores allow registration in ENGL 1102 without ENGL 1101 automatically receive ENGL 1101 credit on successful completion of ENGL 1102. Catalog rules carried in choice notes: (a) a grade of C or better is required in CS 1120, CS 1121, CS 1550 and MATH 1760 before registration in 2000-level CS courses; (b) a minimum grade of C is required to graduate in CS 1120, CS 1121, CS 1550, CS 2100, CS 2240, CS 2230, MATH 1170, MATH 1760, MATH 1750; (c) the two Science-with-Lab courses must come from two different disciplines (approved list: Biology, Botany, Chemistry, Environmental Science, Geography, Geology, Physics, Soils); (d) the four Major Technical Electives (12 credits) must be CS 3000/4000-level or CYB 3000/4000-level courses EXCEPT CS 3980, CS 4000, CS 4010, CS 4310, CS 4990, CYB 4000, CYB 4010, CYB 4800, CYB 4810, CYB 4980, CYB 4990; (e) Statistics: STAT 3010 Probability and Statistics OR STAT 2510 Statistical Methods (one course required). Prereq arrays are left empty: the catalog degree map publishes no per-course prerequisites (it directs students to advisors and the SIS course browser), so none are inferred.
